promises.label: Rebuild 737 production to 52
promises.commitment: Raise 737 production from 42 to 47, then 52 per month, with increases no earlier than roughly six months apart.
promises.outcomeSummary: Boeing was still stabilizing 737 production at 47 airplanes per month; its financial plan targeted rate 52 in the back half of 2027.

resolved.reason: Boeing’s Q1 2025 earnings-call transcript made the increases conditional on stability without a deadline, so Q3 2026 timing guidance left the original commitment open rather than revised.

missing.what_was_said: Management explicitly conditioned further increases on stability: after moving from 42 to 47, Boeing would stay at that rate until stable. Roughly six months was the fastest contemplated interval, not a guaranteed cadence.
Management said demonstrating performance at 47 was taking longer than expected and that full stabilization would take into 2027.

promises.label: Certify 737 MAX derivatives
promises.commitment: Under the revised engine anti-ice schedule, obtain certification of both the 737-7 and 737-10 in 2026.
promises.outcomeSummary: Both the 737-7 and 737-10 obtained FAA certification within 2026; Boeing announced the final certification on Oct. 20, 2026.

citations.title: U.S. FAA certifies Boeing 737-10, largest member of 737 MAX family - Oct 20, 2026

promises.label: Reset 777-9 first-delivery timetable
promises.commitment: Under the October 2025 schedule reset, deliver the first 777-9 in 2027 rather than 2026.
promises.outcomeSummary: Boeing retained its 2027 first-delivery target for the 777-9; the commitment remained pending, with certification still underway.

missing.what_was_said: Boeing's financial-planning targets assumed 777X certification by mid-2027. Management clarified that it was still pursuing earlier certification and had financially provisioned for potential schedule pressure within the EAC. Approval for remaining flight testing, including ETOPS, was still pending. These disclosures qualified, but did not change, the 2027 first-delivery commitment.

promises.label: Reset 787 rate-10 timetable
promises.commitment: Under the post-restart ramp plan, increase 787 production to 10 airplanes per month during 2026.
promises.outcomeSummary: 787 production remained at 8 per month; transition to 10 per month was still expected this year, with engine deliveries pacing the increase.

missing.what_was_said: Boeing temporarily slowed the 787 production system for several days in April to allow parts of the supply chain to recover, and said production would advance only when the system and supply chain were ready.
Management maintained its forecast of 90–100 787 deliveries in 2026, but expected deliveries closer to the lower end because of delays in reaching rate 10.

promises.label: Restore positive annual free cash flow
promises.commitment: Generate positive full-year 2026 free cash flow of $1 billion to $3 billion.
promises.outcomeSummary: Boeing narrowed its 2026 free cash flow outlook to approximately $2 billion; full-year delivery remained pending.
